input.quote: Customer agrees that M&I will have the opportunity to bid on and be considered for all software development, maintenance and other technology projects related to the Services that Customer wishes to implement.
input.rationale: Searches across the Agreement for most-favoured-nation phrasings ("most favored nation", "no less favorable", "favourable/favorable", "best price", "match", "first refusal", "other customers", "third party") return no clause requiring Customer to extend M&I terms no less favourable than those given to any third party or to match third-party offers. The only adjacent provision is Section 18.4, which gives M&I an opportunity to bid on and be considered for technology projects; that is a right to be considered, not an obligation on Customer to grant M&I best terms or to beat competing offers, and it is addressed (if at all) under exclusivity/right-to-bid rules rather than this one. The Agreement therefore meets the preferred position of no MFN obligation burdening Customer, and no redline is warranted.
